context.title: The Great Confession
context.summary: The people fast and confess, and the Levites lead a long prayer retelling Israel's history — God's faithfulness at every stage and the people's repeated rebellion — ending in a written covenant.
context.background: The prayer moves from creation through Abraham, the Exodus, Sinai, the wilderness, the conquest, the judges and the prophets to the exile. Even back in their land, the people say, 'we are servants this day' (v. 36), because Persian kings take the land's produce.

customs.note: Rough goat-hair cloth and dust on the head were signs of mourning and repentance.

watchFor: God is 'ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger' (v. 17).
The refrain of mercy: God did not forsake them (vv. 17, 19, 31).

w: and they cried out to you

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Kadmiel
people.summary: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

people.name: Hodijah
people.summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

people.name: Hashabniah
people.summary: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Sihon
people.summary: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them.

people.name: Og
people.summary: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13).

places.name: Ur
places.summary: Light, or the moon city, a city “of the Chaldees,” the birthplace of Haran (Gen. 11:28, 31), the largest city of Shinar or northern Chaldea, and the principal commercial centre of the country as well as the centre of political power.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Red sea
places.summary: The sea so called extends along the west coast of Arabia for about 1,400 miles, and separates Asia from Africa. It is connected with the Indian Ocean, of which it is an arm, by the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: mount Sinai
places.summary: Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus.

places.name: Bashan
places.summary: Light soil, first mentioned in Gen. 14:5, where it is said that Chedorlaomer and his confederates “smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth,” where Og the king of Bashan had his residence.

places.name: Heshbon
places.summary: Intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Josh. 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Num. 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Josh. 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37).

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.
